 Cinema Dorothy: A Greek name, a story of identity and the freedom to be yourself 
Dorothy has become a symbol of self-discovery, acceptance and the courage to embrace one's true identity
 Keerthy Suresh as the titular character in Dorothy P Sangeetha Updated on :  05 Nov 2026, 6:01 pm 2 min read 
 Copied 
 Karthik Subbaraj’s latest outing Dorothy might have become the talk of town today, but not many know that the word is a feminine name of Greek origin, meaning ‘gift of god’. Beyond its literal meaning, the name is also associated with the freedom to discover, embrace and become one's true self. Interestingly, this idea of self-acceptance is what Karthik Subbaraj delves into his latest film, particularly through the journey of the protagonist, Subbu (played by Sananth). As his decision to embrace his femininity becomes a powerful exploration of identity, rejection and acceptance, the title deems fit!
 The story behind Dorothy: Identity, femininity and the courage to be yourself 
 A still from Dorothy Subbu’s journey is not just about expressing a feminine side; it is about finding the courage to acknowledge a part of himself that society may find difficult to understand. When he first decides to embrace his femininity, his choice is met with rejection, including his best friend Karthi (played by Rishikanth). The people around him, including his family, struggle to accept a version of Subbu that challenges their expectations of masculinity. Their reaction reflects a familiar social tendency: to celebrate individuality only when it remains within the boundaries of what is considered normal. The only person who accepts him for what he is, is his sister-in-law, interestingly named Dorothy, played by Keerthy Suresh.
  However, as the narrative progresses, rejection gradually gives way to acceptance. This shift is significant because it suggests that the problem does not lie in Subbu's identity but in the prejudices through which others perceive him. His eventual acceptance by Karthi becomes a reminder that understanding another person begins when we move beyond rigid ideas of gender and identity. And the song Muthumani celebrates this homecoming.
 Karthi accepts and embraces Subbu as a woman in the film This is where the meaning of Dorothy becomes particularly relevant. If Dorothy represents the ‘gift of God’, Subbu’s femininity can be seen as a gift of individuality — an intrinsic part of who he is, rather than something that needs to be corrected or concealed. The idea of freedom to become oneself further strengthens this connection. True freedom is not merely the ability to make choices; it is the freedom to exist without constantly seeking permission or approval.
  Through Subbu, Karthik Subbaraj brings attention to the emotional complexities of self-expression and the importance of acceptance. Much like the deeper symbolism associated with Dorothy, his journey reminds us that every individual deserves the space to discover and embrace their identity.
